analysis.title: Global Rates Trader: From Hawkish Risk to Risk-Off
key_insights: Risk-off has returned to rates and undone much of the earlier US-led hawkish repricing across global front-ends. GS baseline of steady growth and disinflation points to gradual relief rather than sharply lower yields.
A deeper challenge to the AI trade would change that baseline, because the AI buildout underpins broader optimism and the market's pricing of durably higher policy rates.

US: firm macro data, hawkish Fedspeak and equity turbulence have produced lower growth pricing, sustained hawkish policy pricing and a pronounced tightening in financial conditions. GS sees belly (5y) outperformance as likely and the implied policy path as too hawkish if current inflation pricing holds.
GS recommends buying 3m5y USD receivers against 3m2y receivers, weighted by implied vol, with about 12.5% extra DV01 on the 3m5y leg. Entry 0bp, target 15bp, stop -8bp.

MBS index convexity fell to around zero after the autumn selloff, which reduces convexity-hedging that amplifies selloffs. Convexity is more likely to add a tailwind to duration in large rallies, and 10y tail implied vol has tended to underperform shorter expiries afterward.

Treasury swap spreads: front-end spreads are at fair value and long-end spreads are slightly wide to fair, so there is no clear valuation case for long spread positions. Funding has been tighter since mid-October and risk-off could challenge carry trades, with easing in funding not expected to matter until Q2 and into Q3 of next year.

Canada: BoC rhetoric is hawkish while data are dovish, with all core inflation metrics at or below 2% yoy. GS says a December hike risk has risen but expects any hawkish impulse to front-load tightening rather than extend the peak, so it favors front-end flatteners and 1y1y forward longs.

Europe: GS favors Bund longs. The German curve bear-flattened on spillovers from abroad with little domestic news, euro area growth is expected to soften through H1 2027, and hawkish news should deepen flattening and insulate the belly and longer forwards. GS forecasts the 10y German yield at 3.10% by year-end.

European sovereign spreads remain near year-to-date wides. Lower oil and gas prices after the US midterms and easing French political risk are tailwinds, but sustained tightening needs lower inflation risk and fiscal reassurance, which GS expects to take time given the 2027 French and Italian elections.

UK: the gilt selloff of the past two weeks reflected hawkish BoE commentary and spillovers from the strong US CPI print, while domestic data were softer. GS sees cumulative pricing through February as too hawkish, favors receiving on further selloffs and curve steepeners, and forecasts the 10y gilt at 4.8% by end-2027.

Scandinavia and Switzerland: GS expects two more Riksbank hikes to 2.5% in 2027 and keeps a SEK flattening bias. Norway's September hike to 4.5% likely marked the peak, with cuts from Q4 2027 and a preference for steeper NOK curves relative to SEK. The SNB is expected to hold at 0% through 2027.

Japan: GS expects the BoJ to hike faster than market pricing, which should flatten the JGB curve. It recommends 2s10s JGB flatteners with entry 94bp, target 75bp and stop 105bp. The JGB slope has moved with equities and yields abroad, which limits steepening risk in a risk-off move.

Australia and New Zealand: a weak employment report drove the sharpest single-day AUD rates rally in two years, but firm wages and an unemployment rate below the RBA's NAIRU estimate mean front-end pricing has run ahead of data. GS prefers AUD longs in the belly of the curve and still sees value in paying February RBA OIS as a hedge. In New Zealand it prefers curve steepeners over outright longs.

GS trade book: four active trades are the CHF 1y1y vs EUR 1y1y payer, 2s10s NZD steepeners, 2s10s JGB flatteners and 3m5y vs 3m2y USD receivers. Two stop-outs were closed on 20 November: pay February RBA at -4bp, and earlier long 10y TIPS vs short nominals at -7bp on 17 November.

macro_indicators.interpretation: GS sees a constrained range for Bund yields in its 2027 outlook, with Bunds expected to outperform in global selloffs.
Relief from lower energy prices and less hawkish policy pricing is expected to extend into longer maturities, limited by fiscal uncertainty around next year's Spending Review.
A December hike would more likely pull forward the final move than raise the terminal rate, so GS sees cumulative pricing through February as too hawkish.

macro_indicators.reading: all core metrics at or below 2% yoy
macro_indicators.interpretation: A soft print that contrasts with hawkish BoC rhetoric and supports GS's view that tightening is front-loaded rather than extended.
The sharpest single-day AUD rates rally in two years after a weak employment report, though GS says front-end pricing has run ahead of the data.
Firm wages keep alive the risk that the RBA stays vigilant on broadening inflation pressure.
Next week's print is a fresh upside catalyst for front-end yields.
GS believes the September hike was the peak, with cuts expected from Q4 2027.
GS economists expect two further hikes in 2027, supporting a SEK flattening bias.
An unchanged SNB rate should limit the scope for a sustained selloff in Swiss bonds, though Swiss bonds should lag in rallies.

trade_ideas.description: Buy 3m5y USD receivers versus 3m2y USD receivers, weighted by implied vol (about 12.5% additional DV01 on the 3m5y leg). Entry 0bp, target 15bp, stop -8bp.
trade_ideas.rationale: Equity drawdowns and rate-driven financial conditions tightening have tended to bring forward-curve flattening, which favors the belly over the front end.
trade_ideas.risk: Inflation news and Fed communication may limit how much the very front end participates in rallies.

trade_ideas.description: Add 2s10s JGB curve flatteners. Entry 94bp, target 75bp, stop 105bp.
trade_ideas.rationale: GS economists expect the BoJ to hike faster than priced, and the starting levels of 2s5s and 5s10s are steep relative to macro drivers.
trade_ideas.risk: Greater risk-off or fiscal sustainability concerns, for example growth worries interrupting BoJ tightening or the late-December budget reviving fiscal concerns.

trade_ideas.description: Long Bunds, with favorable risk-reward given softer euro area growth, lower realized vol and limited domestic hawkish news.
trade_ideas.rationale: Global pressures bear-flattened the German curve despite little domestic news, and Bunds should outperform in global selloffs.
trade_ideas.risk: Geopolitics and risk asset performance remain important considerations for duration.

trade_ideas.description: UK curve steepeners and receiving gilt rates on further selloffs, with 10y gilts forecast at 4.8% by end-2027.
trade_ideas.rationale: Cumulative pricing through February looks too hawkish and the UK front end has underperformed its beta to energy prices.
trade_ideas.risk: A December BoE hike, and fiscal uncertainty around the Spending Review limiting long-end compression.

trade_ideas.description: Canada front-end flatteners and 1y1y forward longs.
trade_ideas.rationale: Hawkish BoC rhetoric against soft data should front-load tightening rather than extend the peak, and labor slack is slowing non-shelter inflation.
trade_ideas.risk: Hawkish BoC rhetoric raises the chance of a sequential December hike.

trade_ideas.description: Steeper NOK curves relative to SEK, with a SEK flattening bias.
trade_ideas.rationale: Norway's hike cycle likely peaked with little steepening since, while the Riksbank is expected to hike gradually in 2027.
trade_ideas.risk: Lingering inflation risks in Norway constrain the pace of cuts.

trade_ideas.description: AUD rate longs anchored in the belly of the curve, with paying February RBA OIS as a front-end hedge after the stop-out.
trade_ideas.rationale: The AUD rally has staying power given softer growth, but front-end pricing has run ahead of data.
trade_ideas.risk: Firm wages, an October CPI energy reacceleration and an unemployment rate below NAIRU keep the RBA vigilant.

trade_ideas.description: NZD curve steepeners rather than outright longs (active 2s10s NZD steepeners).
trade_ideas.rationale: GS expects the RBNZ tightening path to eventually underdeliver relative to current market pricing.
trade_ideas.risk: A December RBNZ hike is back on the table after the recent pause.

risk_factors: A deeper challenge to the AI trade would change the baseline given the AI buildout's importance to broader optimism and to the market's pricing of higher policy rates.
Inflation news and Fed communication may limit front-end participation in US rallies.
Higher funding volatility, from bill supply, TGA and weak money fund demand, could challenge carry expressions.
A December BoC hike despite soft core inflation and labor market weakness.
A December BoE hike would be a risk to GS's February baseline.
Fiscal uncertainty in Japan, the UK and France and Italy ahead of 2027 elections.
Growth concerns interrupting the BoJ tightening cycle.
Australian October CPI energy-driven reacceleration and firm wages could push front-end yields higher.
Debt limit timing could affect T-bill supply and funding conditions.
charts_described: Exhibit 1: Distribution of 3m changes in 1y1y/2y1y controlling for change in 1y1y over the last 5y shows equity drawdowns (SPX down at least 5%) with a stronger tendency for forward curves to flatten than implied by their beta to front-end rates.
Exhibit 2: Average 1m change in the 2s5s curve conditioned on 2y yield move since 2000 shows a strong flattening tendency in the month following rate-driven FCI tightening.
Exhibit 3: Change in index MBS duration for potential yield changes shows large yield moves in either direction would bring a duration bid from convexity hedgers, albeit small notional.
Exhibit 4: MBS index convexity versus the residual of 1y10y implied vol shows the 1y10y vol has tended to decline by more than implied by the broader surface after convexity peaks around zero.
Exhibit 5: Cumulative shocks for 2y G4 yields, recentred around US CPI week, show Germany importing bearish pressures from abroad amid limited hawkish domestic news.
Exhibit 6: Residual of GBP 2y OIS regressed on Brent, standardized, shows the UK front end recently disconnected from energy prices, with OIS underperforming its energy beta.
Exhibit 7: Beta of the 2s10s JGB curve to the 2y JGB yield, SPX and the 10y UST yield shows the curve slope has been directional with equities and yields abroad.
vol_and_positioning: MBS index convexity fell to around zero after the autumn selloff, reducing convexity-hedging flows that amplify selloffs and adding a potential duration bid in large rallies.

1y10y implied vol has tended to decline by more than implied by the broader surface after periods where MBS convexity peaks around zero. GS notes 10y tail vol has subsequently underperformed shorter expiries.
GS sees the clearest route to higher vol via large rallies, since tighter policy expectations are largely priced in and growth concerns cap sharp moves back up in yields.
Treasury swap spread vol has been fairly low despite elevated macro risk and volatility in outright yields.
Positioning monitor: GS US Option Implied Position indicator and Data Response Indicator both read 0, and the GS Fund Positioning Indicator reads -2.

CFTC duration-weighted positions show speculators net short across SFR, TU, FV, TY, TN, US and WN, and leveraged funds net short in every contract shown. Asset managers and others are net long in all except SFR, where the position is close to flat.
Greater risk-off could lift money fund AUM and support bill absorption, but would challenge carry trades more generally.
geopolitical: Oil and gas prices fell meaningfully after the US midterm elections, which GS cites as a tailwind for European sovereign spreads.
French political risk has ebbed after OAT outperformance on 17 November, following a modest shift in the RN's position on the pension system.
Political clarity is unlikely until the 2027 elections in France and Italy are over.
UK fiscal uncertainty around next year's Spending Review limits compression in long-end term premia.
Japan's budget proposal in late December 2026 could revive fiscal concerns.

tension_points.bull_case: GS baseline of steady growth and disinflation points to relief over time as inflation progress shifts policy risks and reinforces bonds' hedge value.
tension_points.bear_case: Deeper challenges to the AI trade would change that calculus given the importance of the AI buildout to broader optimism and to markets pricing durably higher policy rates.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A deeper challenge to the AI trade, which would undermine the baseline of gradual relief.

tension_points.bull_case: A weak employment report drove the sharpest single-day AUD rates rally in two years, and a softer growth outlook gives AUD longs relatively compelling asymmetry versus G10.
tension_points.bear_case: Wages were firmer than anticipated, unemployment remains below the RBA's NAIRU estimate and October CPI is likely to show an energy-driven reacceleration.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Next week's October CPI showing an energy-driven reacceleration, which provides a fresh upside catalyst for front-end yields.

tension_points.bull_case: GS economists expect the BoJ to hike faster than priced, containing back-end risk premium and flattening the 2s10s curve toward other G4 curves.
tension_points.bear_case: Greater risk-off or fiscal sustainability concerns could interrupt the BoJ tightening cycle or revive fiscal worries.
tension_points.what_invalidates: 2s10s JGB reaching the 105bp stop, or growth concerns interrupting BoJ tightening, or the late-December 2026 budget proposal reviving fiscal concerns.

theme_stances.key_argument: Firm macro data, Fedspeak and financial conditions tightening bode well for 5y outperformance, and the implied policy path looks too hawkish if inflation pricing is borne out.
Softer euro area growth and the sovereign spread overhang point to more constrained European duration selloffs.
A more hawkish-than-priced BoJ path should flatten the JGB curve.
theme_stances.evidence: argues for a flatter 2s10s JGB curve
